## 🔗 Related Issue
Closes #4106

---

## 📝 Summary

Fixed RBAC visibility inconsistency where non-platform admin users with `is_admin=True` and `platform_admin` role could not see private tools/gateways, despite having admin privileges. Only the bootstrap admin (`PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAIL`) had full visibility.

**Root Cause**: The admin bypass logic required both `user_email=None` AND `token_teams=None`, but logged-in admin users always have their email set, so the bypass never triggered for them.

**Solution**: Added database-backed admin checks to all visibility filtering locations with fail-closed error handling. Now any user with `is_admin=True` in the database gets unrestricted visibility, consistent with the platform admin.

  - resource_service.py: _check_resource_access, subscribe_events
  - a2a_service.py: _check_agent_access
  - tag_service.py: _apply_visibility_scope
  - completion_service.py: _apply_visibility_scope (also fixed missing db parameter)
  - gateway_access.py: check_gateway_access

Test Updates:

- Fixed async test patterns in A2A service tests

Security Properties:
- Fail-closed: Returns False on any exception
- Platform admin priority: Checks PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAIL first
- Explicit boolean check: Handles MagicMock truthy behavior
- Consistent behavior: All admin users get unrestricted visibility

commits.message:
fix(rbac): guard admin bypass with token_teams, extract shared helper

Addresses in-depth review findings on PR #4107.

Blocking fixes:

1. Admin bypass + narrowed token (token_teams=[] or ["t1"]) previously
   granted full Layer-1 visibility because the DB admin check fired
   before the public-only / team-scope guard.  This broke the contract
   in normalize_token_teams() (auth.py) that narrowed tokens must
   constrain even admins — see AGENTS.md token-scoping tables.  Every
   admin-bypass site now requires ``token_teams is None`` before
   consulting DB admin status.

2. tag_service.get_entities_by_tag() did not pass ``db=db`` to
   _apply_visibility_scope(), silently hiding private-tagged entities
   from DB admins (partial reintroduction of #4106).  ``db`` is now
   required on the helper so this cannot happen again.

Design/maintainability fixes:

- Extracted the admin-check policy to mcpgateway/utils/admin_check.py.
  Previously duplicated in BaseService._is_user_admin,
  BaseService._apply_visibility_scope inline, and
  gateway_access.check_gateway_access inline.  All three now delegate
  to one implementation.
- BaseService._apply_visibility_scope is now a @staticmethod with
  required ``db``, removing the BaseService.__new__(BaseService) hack
  in completion_service and tag_service.
- Added request-scoped memoization on ``Session.info``, avoiding N+1
  admin lookups inside loops such as flush_events iterating over
  per-agent visibility checks.
- Added explicit type hints (Select, Type[Any]) on the helper.

Test coverage:

- Deny-path regressions for "DB admin + token_teams=[]" (public-only)
  and "DB admin + token_teams=['x']" (narrowed) across tool, prompt,
  resource, a2a, and gateway services.
- Regression test for tag_service.get_entities_by_tag admin bypass.
- Updated existing admin-bypass tests to use token_teams=None (the
  only scope in which DB admin bypass is permitted).

Signed-off-by: Jonathan Springer <jps@s390x.com>

fix(test): init session affinity in GET replay test to prevent flaky 503

The test_handle_streamable_http_get_replays_from_last_event_id test was missing init_session_affinity(), causing a 503 when the SessionAffinity singleton wasn't pre-initialized by a sibling test on the same xdist worker.
